title: PM SVANidhi Completes One Year of Restructuring: Expanding Credit, Digital Inclusion and Livelihoods Opportunities
body_text:
The Prime Minister Street Vendor’s AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) Scheme , launched on 1 June 2020 to provide collateral-free working capital loans to urban street vendors, has completed one year of its restructured phase. Approved by the Union Cabinet on 27 August 2025 , the lending under the restructured Scheme has been extended up to 31 March 2030 , with an enhanced focus on formal credit, digital financial inclusion, social security, capacity building and entrepreneurship. It aims to benefit 1.15 crore street vendors, including 50 lakh new beneficiaries .
During the first-year post restructuring, 21.86 lakh loans have been disbursed to 10.56 lakh new beneficiaries , amounting to ₹6,294 crore .
To deepen access to formal credit, an UPI-linked RuPay Credit Card with a credit limit of up to ₹30,000 has been introduced for eligible vendors. So far, 27,077 credit cards have been approved .
The introduction of an end-to-end Digital Lending Platform (DLP) has simplified loan processing, from application and verification to approval and disbursement. A Vendor Migration Module has been developed to enable seamless transfer of Letter of Recommendations when vendors migrate between ULBs and Census Towns, ensuring continuity of scheme benefits.
The Scheme with its City Region Approach is expanding its reach by including Census Towns , enabling more street vendors to enter the formal credit and livelihood support ecosystem.
PM SVANidhi has evolved beyond credit delivery towards enterprise development and innovation . The ongoing PM SVANidhi Startup Challenge encourages startups and innovators to develop solutions in areas such as market access, digital payments, financial services, logistics and vending infrastructure.
To improve vending infrastructure and livelihoods, 50 Street Food Hubs (SFHs) will be developed across the country, with cities eligible for financial assistance of up to ₹4 crore per hub , including additional ₹25 lakh for notification of vending zones .
To strengthen last-mile outreach, Lok Kalyan Melas are being organised to bring street vendors, banks and Urban Local Bodies together and facilitate access to credit, welfare schemes and capacity-building programmes. The next round of Lok Kalyan Melas will be organised from 1 September to 30 September 2026 .
Since inception, PM SVANidhi has enabled 78.68 lakh street vendors to access more than 1.18 crore loans , amounting to ₹19,171 crore . To incentivise timely repayment of loans, ₹421 crore has been released as interest subsidy . Further, 57.09 lakh vendors have undertaken over 908 crore digital transactions . Under SVANidhi se Samridhhi, socio-economic profiling of more than 51.15 lakh beneficiaries’ families have been completed and, more than 1.59 crore scheme sanctions have been done under the select 8 central government welfare schemes to the eligible members. Digital adoption has been strengthened through cashback incentives covering both retail and wholesale transactions, with ₹418.78 crore released so far. Till date, more than 6 lakh street food vendors have also received FSSAI training on food safety and hygiene.
PM SVANidhi has thus evolved from a credit intervention into a comprehensive livelihood and entrepreneurship initiative , integrating formal credit, digital inclusion, social security, capacity building, innovation and improved vending infrastructure. The progress in the first year of the restructured phase reflects the Government’s continued commitment to enabling street vendors to become financially empowered, digitally included and socially secure micro-entrepreneurs , contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 .

enrichment.summary: PM SVANidhi, the collateral-free micro-credit scheme for street vendors launched in June 2020, has completed one year of its restructured phase approved by the Cabinet on 27 August 2025, which extends lending till 31 March 2030 and targets 1.15 crore vendors including 50 lakh new beneficiaries. In this first year, 21.86 lakh loans worth ₹6,294 crore were disbursed to 10.56 lakh new beneficiaries, alongside new features such as a UPI-linked RuPay credit card, a digital lending platform, Street Food Hubs, and expansion to Census Towns. Since inception, the scheme has disbursed over 1.18 crore loans worth ₹19,171 crore to 78.68 lakh vendors.
enrichment.context:
PM SVANidhi (Prime Minister Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi) was launched in mid-2020 to provide collateral-free working capital loans to urban street vendors whose livelihoods were disrupted by COVID-19 lockdowns. It has since become one of the flagship urban livelihood schemes under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, complementing the National Urban Livelihoods Mission's focus on the informal urban workforce. The 2025 restructuring reflects a policy shift from a pandemic-relief credit instrument towards a comprehensive micro-entrepreneurship and social security framework for vendors, integrating digital financial inclusion (UPI-RuPay cards, digital lending platforms), convergence with welfare schemes (SVANidhi se Samridhi), skilling (FSSAI food safety training), and infrastructure development (Street Food Hubs, vending zones).

The scheme's 'City Region Approach' extending coverage to Census Towns is notable because it recognises that urbanisation in India is increasingly occurring in un-notified or transitional settlements not covered by statutory Urban Local Bodies. This aligns with broader debates on India's urban governance gaps and the need to extend formal credit and welfare access beyond municipal boundaries. The scheme also ties into the government's digital push, using UPI and RuPay infrastructure to formalise micro-transactions among informal workers, and links to the Viksit Bharat @2047 vision of inclusive economic growth.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the PM SVANidhi Scheme:
1. It was launched in 2020 to provide collateral-free working capital loans to street vendors.
2. The restructured scheme, approved in 2025, extends lending under the scheme up to 31 March 2030.
3. The scheme is implemented exclusively within statutory Urban Local Body limits and excludes Census Towns.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: PM SVANidhi was launched in 2020 and its restructured phase (approved August 2025) extends lending to 2030. Statement 3 is incorrect since the scheme's City Region Approach now includes Census Towns, not just statutory ULBs.

prelims_questions.question: Under the restructured PM SVANidhi Scheme, what is the credit limit of the UPI-linked RuPay Credit Card introduced for eligible street vendors?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that an UPI-linked RuPay Credit Card with a credit limit of up to ₹30,000 has been introduced for eligible vendors under the restructured scheme.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of formal credit and digital financial inclusion in improving the livelihoods of urban street vendors in India. Evaluate the role of schemes like PM SVANidhi in this context.

Examine how the 'City Region Approach' under PM SVANidhi, which extends coverage to Census Towns, addresses gaps in urban governance and livelihood support for informal workers in India's rapidly urbanising landscape.

study_notes.reason: The release carries a solid factual core on scheme parameters (launch date, restructuring approval, targets, tranche structure) that UPSC could test directly, while also offering genuine analytical material on the scheme's evolution from pandemic relief to comprehensive micro-entrepreneurship framework and urban governance gaps around Census Towns.

prelims.point: PM SVANidhi launched 1 June 2020; restructured phase approved by Union Cabinet on 27 August 2025, extending lending till 31 March 2030
prelims.why_important: Core dates and validity period of a flagship urban livelihood scheme are prime targets for factual/chronology-based questions.

prelims.point: Restructured PM SVANidhi targets 1.15 crore street vendors including 50 lakh new beneficiaries
prelims.why_important: Specific numerical targets of the scheme are commonly tested in statement-based prelims questions.

prelims.point: UPI-linked RuPay Credit Card introduced under the scheme with credit limit up to ₹30,000
prelims.why_important: Tests awareness of specific financial instruments/features embedded in welfare schemes.

prelims.point: PM SVANidhi is administered under Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, distinct from rural livelihood schemes under Ministry of Rural Development
prelims.why_important: UPSC frequently tests correct ministry-scheme matching; vendors' scheme could be confused with NULM or rural credit schemes.

prelims.point: 'City Region Approach' expands scheme coverage to Census Towns, not just statutory Urban Local Bodies
prelims.why_important: Distinction between Census Towns (statistical, non-notified) and Statutory Towns (ULB-governed) is a classic prelims confusion point in urban governance.

prelims.point: SVANidhi se Samridhi links vendor beneficiaries to 8 select central welfare schemes through socio-economic profiling
prelims.why_important: Tests knowledge of scheme convergence mechanisms, a recurring theme in welfare scheme questions.

mains.point: Restructuring reflects a policy shift from pandemic-relief credit instrument to a comprehensive micro-entrepreneurship and social security framework
mains.analytical_use: Useful for 'Discuss how welfare schemes evolve from crisis response to structural policy instruments' type questions on scheme design and policy learning.

mains.point: Expansion to Census Towns highlights the gap in India's urban governance framework where transitional settlements lack statutory ULB coverage
mains.analytical_use: Deployable in questions on challenges of extending formal credit/welfare to India's rapidly urbanising but under-governed peri-urban areas.

mains.point: Integration of digital financial tools (UPI-RuPay, Digital Lending Platform) with informal sector credit reflects the government's digital financial inclusion push for micro-entrepreneurs
mains.analytical_use: Can support answers on formalising the informal economy through digital infrastructure (JAM trinity-style analysis).

mains.point: Scheme convergence with skilling (FSSAI training) and welfare schemes represents a move towards holistic livelihood security rather than isolated credit delivery
mains.analytical_use: Useful for 'suggest measures' questions on improving effectiveness of livelihood schemes through inter-scheme convergence.

low_priority.point: Lok Kalyan Melas scheduled for September 2026 and specific figures like ₹421 crore interest subsidy, ₹418.78 crore cashback
low_priority.reason: Administrative/operational detail and cumulative figures without independent significance beyond illustrating scale.

low_priority.point: PM SVANidhi Startup Challenge encouraging innovators in vending-related solutions
low_priority.reason: Promotional initiative with no defined structure or examinable specifics provided.

related_articles.relationship: Both releases mark anniversaries of financial inclusion schemes for underprivileged groups (street vendors vs. unbanked citizens) that rely on RuPay cards and digital banking infrastructure to expand credit access.
